# Consistency review

The live PR matched the dispatched head repository, branch, and SHA before review. Generated output
and CI-only issues were excluded from the inventory.

## Ordered inventory

### I-001 — Dedicated default-disabled test task

- Changed code: `instrumentation/resilience4j-circuitbreaker-2.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:39`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/hystrix-1.4/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:35`
- Frequency: unique
- Disposition: needed
- Rules and precedence: the repository's instrumentation-testing guidance and the module's
  `disabled_by_default` metadata take precedence over raw task frequency.
- Conflict analysis: the Hystrix module demonstrates a dedicated configuration test task, but this
  module uniquely needs a second task that leaves an opt-in instrumentation disabled.
- Rationale: the normal test task explicitly enables the instrumentation, so a separate unconfigured
  task is needed to exercise the declared default.

### F-001 — Class-level suppressions for single advice methods

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/resilience4j-circuitbreaker-2.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/resilience4j/circuitbreaker/v2_0/CircuitBreakerDecoratorsInstrumentation.java:60`,
  `:71`, `:82`, `:115`, `:127`, `:138`;
  `instrumentation/resilience4j-circuitbreaker-2.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/resilience4j/circuitbreaker/v2_0/CircuitBreakerStateMachineInstrumentation.java:97`,
  `:109`, `:146`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/gwt-2.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/gwt/v2_0/GwtRpcInstrumentation.java:100`
  and `:102`
- Frequency: common
- Disposition: avoidable
- Rules and precedence: the repository rule requiring `@SuppressWarnings` on the single member that
  needs it overrides the common older class-level advice pattern.
- Conflict analysis: many advice classes use class-level suppression, but those exemplars conflict
  with the explicit scoping rule when only one advice method needs suppression. Advice classes with
  two methods retained class-level suppression.
- Rationale: method-level suppression provides the same warning behavior without suppressing the
  whole nested class.
- Rule-conflict gate: passed; no higher-precedence rule requires class-level suppression.
- Exemplar recheck: the GWT failure advice scopes `unused` directly to its sole advice method.
- Applied occurrences: all nine single-method advice classes in the PR.

### I-002 — Dynamic-proxy decorator adaptation

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/resilience4j-circuitbreaker-2.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/resilience4j/circuitbreaker/v2_0/Resilience4jCircuitBreakerDecorators.java:71`,
  `:84`, `:140`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/kafka/kafka-clients/kafka-clients-2.6/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/kafkaclients/v2_6/KafkaTelemetry.java:94`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: needed
- Rules and precedence: the instrumentation-writing guidance permits decorators; no path-specific
  rule requires concrete wrappers.
- Conflict analysis: concrete wrappers are more common, but they cannot preserve arbitrary
  Resilience4j checked-function interfaces or the full `CompletionStage` surface.
- Rationale: proxy adaptation preserves the library interfaces while routing decorated calls through
  the span lifecycle.

### I-003 — Multiple thread-local correlation stacks

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/resilience4j-circuitbreaker-2.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/resilience4j/circuitbreaker/v2_0/Resilience4jCircuitBreakerSpans.java:28-35`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/spring/spring-cloud-aws-3.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/spring/cloud/aws/v3_0/SpringAwsUtil.java:26`
- Frequency: unique
- Disposition: unclear
- Rules and precedence: no repository consistency rule governs this temporal correlation structure;
  the closest component pattern and raw frequency therefore apply.
- Conflict analysis: the exemplar uses one thread-local correlation container, while this module
  coordinates six stacks. Determining whether they can be consolidated requires functional and
  concurrency review, which is outside this review.
- Rationale: the structure is substantially more complex than the closest compliant pattern, but no
  behavior-preserving consistency-only replacement was established.

### F-002 — Literal semantic-convention exception keys in tests

- Changed code:
  `instrumentation/resilience4j-circuitbreaker-2.0/javaagent/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/resilience4j/circuitbreaker/v2_0/Resilience4jCircuitBreakerTest.java:493`,
  `:495`, `:832`, `:834`, `:916`, `:918`, `:984`, `:986`
- Closest compliant exemplar:
  `instrumentation/hibernate/hibernate-3.3/javaagent/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/hibernate/v3_3/SessionTest.java:12-14`
- Frequency: rare
- Disposition: avoidable
- Rules and precedence: the path-specific semantic-convention rule requires tests to import stable
  constants directly; it overrides literal-key usage.
- Conflict analysis: the local Resilience4j experimental keys have no canonical semconv constants
  and remain literal, while `exception.type` and `exception.message` exactly match stable keys.
- Rationale: `EXCEPTION_TYPE` and `EXCEPTION_MESSAGE` provide identical typed keys without local
  reconstruction.
- Rule-conflict gate: passed; the stable constants have the same names and `AttributeKey<String>`
  types.
- Exemplar recheck: the Hibernate test statically imports and uses both stable exception constants.
- Applied occurrences: all eight literal exception-key constructions in the PR.

No other avoidable consistency findings were identified.
